title: The Last Regiment
premise: In 1849, in the isolated mountain town of Verenchal, apprentice clockmaker Zephyrine Hartwell is summoned to repair the observatory's master clock and discovers hidden inside its mechanism documents proving the garrison commander has been falsifying desertion records to cover a massacre of conscripts. With the bridge closed for winter, she must smuggle the evidence past three checkpoints guarded by men she has spent a lifetime avoiding, aided by a found family of townsfolk who each risk something irreplaceable. The commander, realizing what she carries, turns the town against her through fear and memory manipulation, forcing Zephyrine to choose between the silence that once kept her safe and the truth that could destroy everyone she loves. In the end, she sacrifices her anonymity and nearly her life to send the evidence across the frozen river, and the town, forever changed, begins reckoning with what it chose not to see.
about_author: M. M. Blackwood is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing garrison records in provincial European towns before turning to fiction. Their novels examine how ordinary people survive complicity, and how memory becomes both weapon and refuge.

chapters.title: The Silence in the Gears
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Summoned to the observatory to repair the master clock, she navigates the commander's watchful household, noting which servants speak and which have learned not to. Finding the hidden documents wedged in the clock's escapement, she understands why the mechanism was sabotaged. The emotional beat: dread disguised as professional calm, as her invisibility strategy begins to fail.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Small Doors
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, with flashback texture. She weighs the evidence against her history: an orphan raised by a clockmaker who taught her that survival means being unremarkable. A visit to her aging mentor reveals he knew the clock held something and chose silence too. The beat: the cost of a life built on not-looking, and the first crack in her resolve.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Multiple POV, anchored by Zephyrine. The last cart crosses before the winter closure, and the town contracts into itself. Zephyrine realizes she has until spring thaw to act. She confides partially in Marta, the observatory cook, who reveals her own lost brother among the conscripts. The beat: isolation breaking, the found family beginning to assemble around a shared risk.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints, One Winter
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She maps the route: the garrison gate, the tollhouse, the river watch. She studies the men who staff them, learning their habits as she once learned gears. The commander, Colonel Vasseur, begins quietly asking why the clock needed two repairs. The beat: cold, methodical tension; the reader feels the machinery of surveillance closing around her.

chapters.title: The Tollhouse Keeper's Daughter
chapters.summary: Alternate POV: Ilse, seventeen, tollhouse keeper's daughter, who idolizes the garrison and resents the town. Zephyrine courts her trust with a repaired music box, but Ilse's loyalty is genuine and therefore dangerous. The beat: the ache of manipulating someone who offers real friendship, and Zephyrine's first taste of the corruption she's fighting.

chapters.title: What Vasseur Remembers
chapters.summary: Vasseur's POV. The commander's own memories of the massacre, reframed over years of self-justification, are fraying; he falsifies records partly to keep his version of events intact. He suspects Zephyrine and tightens the checkpoints, using fear to make the townspeople inform on each other. The beat: chilling intimacy with power's self-deception, showing corruption as a form of memory-keeping.

chapters.title: The Night the Bells Stopped
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Vasseur orders the town's bells silenced after a near-discovery, and the silence becomes a weapon — no one may signal anyone. The found family improvises a code through chimney smoke and hymn timing. Marta is detained for questioning. The beat: terror and defiance intertwined; the family chooses each other openly for the first time.

chapters.title: Ilse at the Tollhouse
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. She discovers Zephyrine's deception and the documents' existence, and must choose between the garrison she worshipped and the truth about her father's complicity at the tollhouse. She lets Zephyrine pass the second checkpoint — then is seen doing it. The beat: betrayal inverted into sacrifice; Ilse's coming-of-age as the arc's most costly turn.

chapters.title: The Frozen Crossing
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, climax. With the bridge watched and Ilse detained, Zephyrine attempts the river ice at night, pursued by Vasseur's men. The ice breaks; she nearly drowns, saved by townsfolk who signal with the restored master clock's bells — the town itself becomes her ally. The evidence crosses; she is caught. The beat: peak peril, communal courage, and Vasseur's mask shattering.

chapters.title: Spring Thaw
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, months later. Investigators arrive with the thaw; Vasseur is taken, and Ilse released. Zephyrine, no longer invisible, repairs the town's clocks openly and takes Ilse as an apprentice. The master clock keeps honest time at last. The beat: quiet, earned resolution — memory restored, family chosen, power answered by truth.
